summary.headline: Mahindra Holidays Q2 FY27: standalone PAT fell 16% to INR43 crores on growth costs, even as resort revenue grew 15% and upgrades rose 26%.
summary.overview: Standalone total income rose 4% YoY to INR395 crores, with double-digit resort revenue growth offset by flat membership income, so EBITDA fell 12% to INR124 crores and PAT fell 16% to INR43 crores. Consolidated PAT grew 17% to INR19.7 crores and consolidated total income rose 9% to INR819 crores. Management cited growth-linked costs, renovation downtime, new unprofitable resorts, GST and solar subsidy effects as margin drags. Network shrank to 5,762 keys across 106 resorts after 6 exits, with about 1,000 gross keys targeted over the next six months.

financial_highlights.change: vs INR166 crores a year ago

segments.name: Vacation ownership (VO) / Keystone
segments.commentary: Upgrades grew 25-27% YoY per management; net member additions reported but expected to rise over next 1-2 quarters. Member base about 303,000; organic and digital contributed 66% of additions, with referrals at 40-50% of new sales. 12-month retention rose from about 11%.

segments.name: Resorts (standalone)
segments.commentary: Resort revenue grew 15%, the highest in 8 quarters, with occupancy at 75.6%. Resort margins were pressured by new resorts, renovation downtime, GST and solar subsidy effects.

segments.name: Holiday Club Resorts Oy (HCRO, Finland)
segments.commentary: Revenue grew 8% to EUR 36.5 million; EBITDA EUR 1.7 million (vs EUR 1.3 million); net loss EUR 0.3 million. Loss in Indian books including interest and forex was INR18 crores vs INR27 crores a year ago. Strategic review in progress.

guidance_outlook: About 1,000 gross keys to be added over the next six months; 442 keys currently under renovation expected to return mainly in Q3 and Q4.
Target of 10,000 keys by FY30 is on track; 85% visibility on the target per management, with about 1,500 keys still to be identified (net figure).
Around 650 keys to be exited in FY27 in total, versus about 400 exited last year; management says the exit journey is largely done.
Capex in the next six months to be roughly equal to H1 spend, per management.
H2 expected to be more profitable than H1, with Q3 and Q4 seasonally strongest, especially for non-member business.
Capital allocation about 70% to new resorts and 30% to existing resort improvements.
Occupancy expected to climb in Q3 and Q4; management sees no major West Asia impact on occupancy, though some project costs and delays have emerged.
Upcoming openings: Ganpatipule (Q3 end or Q4 start), Kumbhalgarh (Q3), Jaisalmer (Q3), Gir (Q4 end or Q1 early).
capex_capacity: H1 FY27 capex about INR312 crores, up from INR166 crores a year ago; cash generation in H1 in line with last year.
Network at 5,762 keys across 106 resorts in September after exiting 6 resorts and a net reduction of 103 keys in the quarter.
8 ongoing greenfield and brownfield projects; Poovar recently opened; two transformed properties opened in Q2 and about 5 transformations underway.
Growth capital for capabilities, renovation downtime and new properties estimated at INR9-15 crores per quarter.
Signature Resorts: luxury family and tribe offering, targeted ARR about INR20,000.
demand_pricing: Occupancy 75.6%, up 220 bps YoY; management expects full-year occupancy of 80-81% and rising occupancy into Q3 and Q4 through algorithmic inventory allocation.
Premiumisation: 10-year Ivory is the most preferred Keystone product; 10-year and 5-year together about 80% of the portfolio.
West Asia crisis raised airfares and limited some overseas-linked occupancy, offset by driving holidays; the model is not heavily dependent on overseas travellers.
Cost of acquisition as a percentage of sales declined YoY; management targets sustained reduction.
Non-member, corporate and MICE business growing from a small base.

qa_highlights.question: How is Keystone performing across Ebony, Ivory and Jade, and what are the FY27 expectations for sales and realisations?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the 10-year Ivory product has the most members and the 10-year plus 5-year products make up about 80% of the portfolio. Upgrades grew 25-27% YoY, and net member additions are expected to rise over the next 1-2 quarters, though no formal guidance was given.

qa_highlights.question: How much inventory is out of service for renovation, and when will it return?
qa_highlights.answer: 442 keys are under renovation, with most expected back in Q3 and Q4. No revenue offset was quantified.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a West Asia or inflation-driven slowdown risk for Q3 demand and expansion?
qa_highlights.answer: Some limited occupancy impact from higher airfares, offset by driving holidays. Project costs have risen and some openings are delayed, but no plans are being pulled back.

qa_highlights.question: How is capital allocated between new capacity and existing resorts?
qa_highlights.answer: About 70% toward new resorts and about 30% toward improving existing resorts over the longer term.

qa_highlights.question: What is the H1/H2 revenue split?
qa_highlights.answer: VO membership and ASF income (about two-thirds of revenue) are broadly even across quarters; the remaining third splits about 35-40% in H1 and 60-65% in H2.

qa_highlights.question: Why did standalone EBITDA and PAT fall while resort revenue grew?
qa_highlights.answer: Drags include investments in future capacity, transformation, unprofitable new resorts, GST and solar subsidy effects. Management expects renovated resorts returning and higher volumes to ease margin pressure.

qa_highlights.question: Is the company raising debt to fund capex?
qa_highlights.answer: No. Management plans to rely on internal accruals, with cash of about INR1,300 crores.

risks_watch: Standalone PAT down 16% and EBITDA down 12%; watch whether H2 profitability recovers as renovated keys return.
Project delays and higher delivery costs could slip the 1,000-key addition and the 10,000-key FY30 target.
HCRO remains loss-making; strategic review outcome pending.
Unresolved follow-up on deferred revenue recognition versus the stated run-rate; management deferred the answer offline.
West Asia geopolitical and inflation pressure on travel demand into the December season.
Member-to-room ratio is expected to fall as keys grow, but rationalisation could weigh on metrics for a quarter or two.
summary.management_tone: Confident on top-line metrics such as resort revenue, upgrades, AUR and occupancy, but cautious on profitability, which management explained as temporary investment drag. Evasive on the deferred revenue question and the exact member-addition figures, deferring both offline.
key_quotes: So overall, during the quarter, we exited 6 resorts, taking the network to 5,762 keys across 106 resorts in September.
H2 typically is more profitable for us in any case. And Q2 is usually our worst quarter.
So we are going to rely on the internal accruals for future expansion as well as transformation.

growth.why: Management guides occupancy rising to 80-81% for FY27 and H2 more profitable than H1, backed by about 1,000 gross keys to be added in the next six months and 442 renovated keys returning in Q3-Q4, with a named set of openings; no revenue growth % is guided, and margins remain under pressure from new resorts, renovation downtime and cost items.
